_note: Josh's verdicts on the 27 Aug before/after sheet (compare_layouts --refit). BEFORE = shipped layout, AFTER = pipeline as of commit e357edc. Verbatim; 'verdict' is his comparison, 'themes' are tags for grouping.

verdicts.note: Both clearly wrong. Very complicated roof, this one should probably just have no panels on it at all.
New one looks better, but covering some obstructions which shouldn't be covered.
New one much better.
A little better, but both not very good and not clean layouts with clearly defined roof shape.
Both bad, do not understand the roof shape cleanly. Easy roof shape repeated a few times. There are 8 clear planes, 4 sloping one direction and 4 sloping the other.
A bit better, but definitely not creating a clean and accurate understanding of the roof shape. Need to be able to create a clean 3D planar type roof shape for accurate panel placement.
Better, but some white flat roof areas being ignored that could have panels.
Both bad and not accurately fitting roof shape.
Hard to tell, likely better, but not accounting for some obstructions underneath.
Similar for both, both bad and not clearly understanding the roof shape.
About equal, not clearly defining roof shape.
Better, though placing some strange standalone panels and some panels overlapping edges instead of a clean array.
Similar on both. This is a 3 plane roof not 2 planes; one plane is not being detected, it should be 3 distinct arrays.
Still overlapping roof corner ridges where a roof changes angle by 90 degrees and there is a 45 degree mitre type roof joint. Need to detect those better, they are very common on roof geometry.
Both terrible. Building outlines are fuzzy and unrealistic, clearly not getting a good planar 3D shape of the roof.
Same as 15, clearly not getting a good 3D planar shape of the roof to then accurately place panels.
Both good, but the obstructions placed here are too large; it's a whole area which seems otherwise fine to place panels.

Detecting ridges possibly a bit better, but still not very good; panels overlapping roof ridges and joints, and a strange panel density with lots of singular or 2-3 array panel sections scattered over the roof.
Better, but still placing small panel arrays in random places, and treating a gradually curving sloping roof as two planes when really it is a light curve across the whole roof.

Much better than before, though there is still a strange panel array down the bottom right which shouldn't be there, placed on a section of building that is unrealistic and not part of the main defined roof.
